jobs.occupation: Service Designer, Defence Service Development
jobs.description:
Design the services that keep Defence Forces mission-ready. As a Service Designer, you will shape and sharpen the service offerings that help Defence organisations turn complex C4I capabilities into sustained operational readiness.

The job

You will build on and further develop our existing service offerings across pre-sales, system design, deployment, training, testing and operations. Through service design, systems thinking and deep user understanding, you will strengthen how we package, deliver and support complex C4I capabilities – enabling customers to maintain and enhance their operational readiness.

Your key responsibilities:

• Building on existing service definitions and best practices by analysing customer organisations, operational contexts and delivery experiences to identify improvement opportunities

• Extending and refining the service catalogue by translating input from Sales, service delivery teams and customers into standardized service offerings.

• Improving service blueprints, delivery models and customer journeys with a focus on operational fit, role clarity and predictable outcomes

• Facilitating structured workshops with delivery teams and key stakeholders to align and validate service content

• Strengthening standardised service packages to ensure consistent, repeatable delivery across customers and constellations.

Success in this role means customers move smoothly from initial engagement to effective operational use, are fully prepared to operate our solutions, and sustain their operational capability over time. Your work directly enables Defence organisations to deploy and sustain critical C4I capabilities with confidence.

Joining the team

You'll join our Defence Service Development team in Aarhus, working to continually strengthen the services behind our customers' everyday-ready C4I capabilities. The team brings together service design, military domain knowledge, solution architecture, portfolio management and business analytics. You'll work with strategic projects where an operational mindset is needed, evolving service definitions and delivery models to keep them relevant and effective. You'll report to Marie Lunde Jørgensen, Manager Defence Service Development and collaborate closely with stakeholders across our departments worldwide.

Your qualifications

You hold a relevant master’s degree – ideally in Service System Design, Strategy, Technology-Based Business Development or a similar field – and bring:

• Preferably experience in service design or service development for complex digital solutions, including creating new services and maturing existing ones to support operational delivery

• Experience with refining service definitions and delivery models for complex technical and organisational environments, with a focus on clarity, consistency and reduced operational risk

• Sound knowledge of service design methodologies, such as user journey mapping, service blueprinting and pain-point analysis

• Strong English communication skills, spoken and written, with an independent and structured approach to complex challenges

• Willingness to travel 10-20 days a month

It would also be an advantage if you bring:

• Experience with large-scale enterprise or defence solutions and established delivery organisations

• Familiarity with agile, system-oriented ways of working, focused on continuous improvement and operational outcomes

• Experience with customer success disciplines, and an interest in helping shape our approach to customer success within defence

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks, from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1,100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Marie Lunde Jørgensen, Manager, Defence Service Development.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager, Anaesthesia & Patient Monitoring Solutions

This requires strong project management capabilities, sound business and technical understanding, and broad experience with medical device development.

• Leading medical device development projects of varying scope and complexity, from major new product development initiatives to product enhancements, upgrades and design changes, through to successful implementation at our production sites

• Are comfortable leading projects of different sizes and levels of complexity and can adapt your project management approach accordingly

• Are committed and structured, with a strong sense of responsibility towards your work and your team

• Possess strong leadership skills and are able to create direction, engagement and momentum in cross-functional teams

The Talent Attraction team till engage with applicants on an ongoing basis, hence we encourage you to not hesitate, and apply today!

Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

jobs.occupation: Senior Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
**Create Solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**

**Are you motivated by working with complex commercial contracts, legal risk management and major construction and infrastructure projects in an international environment? Do you enjoy combining strong legal expertise with a pragmatic, business-oriented approach to support decision-making and deliver practical solutions? And do you thrive in a collaborative role where you can build relationships across a global organization? Then COWI could be the right place for you.

**

To support our business in Denmark and internationally, we are looking for a Senior Legal Counsel to join our legal team at COWI's headquarters in Lyngby, Denmark. As an international consultancy, COWI delivers engineering, architecture, energy and environmental solutions across the globe. We contribute to some of the world's most significant and sustainable projects, and our legal team plays an important role in enabling our business, managing legal and commercial risks, and supporting successful project delivery.

In this role, you will report to the Head of Legal responsible for Business Line Denmark. You will join the Danish legal team, consisting of four senior legal counsels and two paralegals, and become part of COWI's Group Legal function. Group Legal comprises 25 team members based in Denmark, Sweden, Norway, the UK, Ireland and Canada, providing comprehensive legal support across COWI's business lines.

This position is ideal for an experienced legal professional who enjoys working hands-on with complex contractual matters, negotiating commercial agreements and supporting large construction and infrastructure projects. You will take ownership of legal matters, provide clear and commercially focused advice, and work closely with colleagues across the organization to manage risk and find practical solutions.

Your key responsibilities

• Providing day-to-day legal advice and assistance to senior management, operational management and project managers in Denmark and internationally.

• Structuring, drafting and negotiating consultancy agreements, framework agreements, joint venture agreements, memoranda of understanding, teaming agreements and other commercial contracts.

• Advising on contract management, claims management and the identification, assessment and mitigation of legal and commercial risks.

• Reviewing and negotiating contracts for large and complex construction and infrastructure projects, including agreements based on ABR 18, AB 18, FIDIC and bespoke contractual terms.

• Providing legal support to ongoing projects throughout their lifecycle, helping project teams navigate contractual obligations, risks and commercial challenges.

• Advising on disputes and settlement negotiations, including instructing and coordinating external legal counsel.

• Supporting, training and guiding line managers and senior management on legal matters, including contracts, public procurement, competition law, intellectual property rights and data protection.

• Supporting corporate housekeeping and advising on legal compliance matters.

• Providing legal support for mergers and acquisitions and other strategic business initiatives.

• Contributing to the continuous improvement and development of COWI's standard contract templates and legal processes.

**Your skills. Our teams. Together we design the future.

**

At COWI, collaboration is essential. We value professionals who build strong relationships, take ownership, and contribute with both technical expertise and a pragmatic, business-oriented mindset. You are proactive, curious and motivated to continuously improve how legal support is delivered across the organization.

On top of that, you will have:

• A Danish Master's degree in Law.

• Experience from a law firm and/or an in-house legal function.

• Extensive experience in contractual review and negotiation, including ABR 18, AB 18, FIDIC and bespoke forms of agreements.

• A strong understanding of legal and commercial risk management, with the ability to identify, assess and mitigate contractual risks.

• Strong drafting and communication skills in both Danish and English.

• Excellent analytical skills and the ability to translate complex legal issues into clear, concise and commercially relevant advice for legal and non-legal stakeholders.

• A pragmatic, business-oriented approach, balancing attention to detail with an understanding of the bigger picture.

• The ability to work independently, take ownership of complex legal matters and make sound, well-reasoned decisions.

• A collaborative mindset and an interest in working as part of a specialist legal team supporting a large international organization.

• Experience working in an international environment would be an advantage.

**A place to work and so much more.

**

At COWI, we collaborate with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow.

We support our customers' transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to set a positive standard by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the solutions we provide for our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun, because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home. With offices primarily located in Scandinavia, the UK, North America and India, we bring together expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and the environment to create lasting impact.

**Got More Questions?

**

If you have any questions about the role or what we have to offer, please contact Head of Legal Denmark, Kit Bækgaard at kich@cowi.com or Senior Global Talent Acquisition Specialist, Mette Gutte at mtgt@cowi.com

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you're interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

**

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths.

We take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting up teams and forums. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: Interdisciplinary Postdoctoral Fellow in Host-Directed Antimicrobial Research
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a one-year position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  Introduction

  Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge that highlights the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotic treatment.

  Host-directed antimicrobial strategies are attracting increasing interest as complementary approaches to conventional antimicrobial therapy. Recent studies have demonstrated that a novel synthetic compound improves survival in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected Caenorhabditis elegans. Furthermore, previous studies in mammalian cells suggest that the compound may exert immunomodulatory effects, raising the possibility that stimulation of host defence pathways contributes to protection against infection.

  This project aims to determine whether the novel synthetic compound can stimulate innate immunity and enhance host defence pathways in C. elegans and thereby contribute to protection against MRSA-infection. Using a combination of immunology, microbiology, and transcriptomics, the successful candidate will lead the experimental investigation of the phenotypic and transcriptional responses underlying this protective effect. All experimental work will be conducted in C. elegans.

  Required qualifications

   	
• A PhD in immunology, infection biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, or a related discipline. 	
• Hands-on experience with the maintenance and experimental use of Caenorhabditis elegans, preferably as an infection model. 	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways. 	
• Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research. 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.   Highly desirable qualifications

   	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans. 	
• Experience with bacterial culture and experimental microbiology. 	
• Experience with omics-data analysis (such as RNA-seq data). 	
• Experience with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and gene expression analysis. 	
• Experience with RNA interference (RNAi) and gene-silencing approaches. 	
• Knowledge of antimicrobial compounds and antimicrobial resistance. 	
• Experience contributing to external funding applications. 	
• A strong publication record relative to career stage.   Key responsibilities

  The postdoctoral fellow will conduct research within host-directed antimicrobial strategies and innate immunity. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to student supervision, assist in the preparation of external funding applications, and lead the dissemination of research findings through scientific publications and presentations, as well as participate in other academic activities.

  Research environment and collaboration 

  The successful candidate will be based in a research environment with expertise in C. elegans biology and will interact closely with collaborators possessing complementary expertise in immunity, microbiology, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the project provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and the development of skills across multiple disciplines while independently driving the research project.

  Further information

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://ivh.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Tina V. A. Hansen, alstrup@sund.ku.dk

  Starting date and duration

  The position is available from 1 March 2027 or after agreement. The position is a fixed-term, full-time postdoctoral appointment for a period of one year.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact information for 2–3 references.   The deadline for applications is Tuesday 24 November 2026, 23:59pm CET

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Drosophila transposon regulation
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a fixed-term 17-month-assistant professor position in the field of transposon and germline genome regulation at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Denmark.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 17-month fixed-term position expected to start on 15 January 2027 with projected end on June 14, 2028.

Job description
As an assistant professor you will be coordinating and executing experimental and analytical research work in the group of Associate Professor Peter Ebert Andersen. You will be responsible for the daily coordination with other group members. 

Your tasks will include:

• Planning and executing experimental work using Drosophila melanogaster and various genomics and proteomics methods
• Analysing data produced by yourself and other group members
• Contributing to the writing of research papers and research applications
 

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in the area of gene regulation and germline biology with a proven track record for high-quality publications in the field.

The following academic and personal qualifications are particularly valued for this position:

• Experience in the use of Drosophila as a model organism
• In-depth knowledge of Drosophila germline development and gene regulation
• Expertise in a broad range of molecular biology techniques, including preparation of various genomics libraries
• Publication experience, ideally also as corresponding author (can be on preprints) 
• A track record of international research collaborations
• Strong communication skills in English (written and verbal)

The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics
The Department is part of the Faculty of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University and comprises research within the areas of Plant Molecular Biology, Neurobiology, RNA Biology & Innovation, Protein Science, Bioinformatics & Computational Biology (BiRC), and Molecular Health. The department currently has 142 full-time scientific staff and 85 PhD students. jobs.occupation: 171626 Associate professor in Clinical Proteomics and Data-Driven Biomarker Discovery for Neurodegenerative Disease (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position:

Find information about each criterion.

• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Desired qualifications: 

   	
• Strong, independent research record in neurodegenerative disease, with expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and biofluid biomarker discovery. 	
• Experience integrating multi-omics data with machine learning and AI, and working with preclinical models and cell-type-resolved approaches. 	
• A track record of securing competitive external funding and of research leadership. 	
• Teaching experience and formal teaching qualifications (e.g. Universitetspædagogikum), together with supervision experience. 	
• Ability to bridge discovery and translation (from molecule to patient) and to collaborate across academia, clinic, and industry, including innovation and spin-out activity   Terms of employment
 The position is a time limited position for 5 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

 Questions

 Foreign applicants may find this link useful: https://www.ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility).
 
 Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application, including motivations for applying for the position (maximum 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates)

• Research plan (3-5 pages)

jobs.description:
About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like

• Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners.

Successful candidates must document:

• Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE)
• Python programming skills
• Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar)
• Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments

The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
